messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] MonteCarlo in Mplusautomation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Zahra,

If you want the individual LL values, you need to run each replication individually as an analysis and extract the results using readModels. The MONTECARLO syntax you have used will take the replications in your list and run each, then compile summary statistics such as mean LL, MSE, etc. (this is a feature of Mplus). Attached is an example of how to run each replication separately, building on the parallel features in R so that you can run as many models simultaneously as you have cores available. Hope this helps! This was written before Josh’s useful mplusModeler was built into the package, so some of the code could be further streamlined to integrate the inline use of Mplus.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: replaceOutfile argument of runModels not behaving as expected
messages.subject_clean: replaceOutfile argument of runModels not behaving as expected
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm calling runModels via the following:

runModels(directory="D:/Dissertation/data", recursive = TRUE, filefilter = "*boot-s.inp", replaceOutfile = "never")

As you can probably tell from the call to runModels, I only want to run the syntax files that end in "boot-s.inp" to run, and then only if they've never been run before. There are 360,000 files to run, nested in 4 levels of folders in the given directory. However, when I quit R after some of them have run and then later start a new session and resume running the models, they always begin again from the beginning! Am I doing something wrong?
